summary.name: Sentinel 2.0 for Windows
summary.one_liner: A self-contained Windows x64 .exe by James Murphy that checks PC hardening, remote access, autoruns, local admin accounts and event logs, then reports findings without changing anything.
use_cases: Checking whether a Windows PC's security settings are turned on
Reviewing which remote-access services are enabled
Auditing autorun entries and scheduled tasks for unexpected startup items
Reviewing local admin accounts on a Windows machine
Producing a Markdown or HTML report of Windows security findings
summary.what_it_does: Sentinel 2.0 for Windows ships as one self-contained Sentinel.exe for Windows x64 that runs without an installer. It checks Microsoft Defender, firewall profiles, UAC, BitLocker, Secure Boot, SMBv1 and LLMNR, plus RDP, WinRM, Remote Registry and remote-management tools. It also reviews autorun entries, scheduled tasks, local admin accounts and key Windows event logs. Files can be compared against public malware hash lists from MalwareBazaar, ThreatFox and URLhaus, and the page says nothing is uploaded from the PC. Findings can be exported as Markdown or HTML, and a complete pass requires running as Administrator.
notable: Single self-contained Sentinel.exe with no installer, for Windows x64
Read-only: reports findings but does not block threats or remove files
Compares files against public malware hash lists (MalwareBazaar, ThreatFox, URLhaus) without uploading anything
Companion Sentinel Native 2.1 is a C++/Rust build with extra blue-team checks
caveats: Unsigned exe; Windows SmartScreen will warn and the user must choose Run anyway
Not a substitute for Microsoft Defender or an EDR product
